steps.name: Zima
steps.text: ...What are you doing, Mykola?

steps.name: Ursine Student A
steps.text: Someone was falling behind—

steps.name: Zima
steps.text: So you decided to break formation on the left flank? Do it over!

steps.name: Zima
steps.text: Good. Advance with your spears and force me into a corner.

steps.name: Ursine Student B
steps.text: You're too strong, Sonya. We can't budge you.

steps.name: Zima
steps.text: It's not that I'm too strong, it's that you are not pushing together.

steps.name: Zima
steps.text: You have to remember, we're not guerillas. The empire will not protect us, so we must form a fortress together.

steps.name: Zima
steps.text: Do you understand?

steps.name: Everyone
steps.text: Yes, ma'am!

steps.name: Leto
steps.text: Hey, General! Still training?

steps.name: Zima
steps.text: You just got back?

steps.name: Zima
steps.text: What's the sitch?

steps.name: Leto
steps.text: Good news, the cannons and heavy weapons they were showing off yesterday are gone.

steps.name: Leto
steps.text: Nika saw the thugs moving a bunch of stuff out. Looked like weapons.

steps.name: Leto
steps.text: Natalya got it done, Sonya.

steps.name: Zima
steps.text: ...I knew we could count on them.

steps.name: Leto
steps.text: Also, like we were talking about, Gromov sleeps in a camp inside the quarantine zone each night. Only Pavlovich lives on top of the walls.

steps.name: Leto
steps.text: We can smash the thugs' main force before we assault the wall.

steps.name: Zima
steps.text: We need more food and other supplies. Did you see their warehouse?

steps.name: Leto
steps.text: No... How much longer can we stretch these rations?

steps.name: Zima
steps.text: Three days, max. The Unbound are running short also. We owe Antosha too much already.

steps.name: Zima
steps.text: I got a bad history with food supplies... I can't—

steps.name: Leto
steps.text: Hold my hand! It'll be okay, General. We'll get through this.

steps.name: Zima
steps.text: We need to keep training. I got a feeling the next few days are gonna decide our fate.

steps.name: Leto
steps.text: Just how many are willing to fight...?

steps.name: Zima
steps.text: Surprisingly many. They've seen our training these last few days pay off. And the rest are willing to do first aid and logistics.

steps.name: Zima
steps.text: There's nothing young people hate more than injustice, is there?

steps.name: Leto
steps.text: You've done a good job, that's all.

steps.name: Leto
steps.text: What about that Fedya? He's not a student. Is he willing to join?

steps.name: Zima
steps.text: Hm... I'm still not sure if we can trust him.

steps.name: Zima
steps.text: We really don't know anything about him. But he is determined.

steps.name: 'Pencil Stub'
steps.text: Fedya! I found a can of meat. Want some?

steps.name: Fedya
steps.text: ...No, thank you.

steps.name: Yeremey
steps.text: Don't push it. You haven't known him that long, you don't know he likes to be alone.

steps.name: 'Pencil Stub'
steps.text: Come on, it's been a few days, we're not exactly strangers anymore.

steps.name: 'Pencil Stub'
steps.text: Say, Fedya, you don't look like a student, but you don't look like a worker either.

steps.name: 'Pencil Stub'
steps.text: How did you ever end up in this hellhole?

steps.name: Fedya
steps.text: ...I'm sorry, but I can't divulge that, under any circumstances.

steps.name: 'Pencil Stub'
steps.text: Whuh?

steps.name: Yeremey
steps.text: Just who the hell...?

steps.name: Witte
steps.text: Time is short, Your Imperial Majesty. I beg you to consider it one last time.

steps.name: Fyodor
steps.text: Consider, yes—I'm considering feeding all these obese geriatrics to flesh buthidas.

steps.name: Fyodor
steps.text: That way, we'd get a windfall for the treasury by confiscating their assets, and a bunch of well-fed, succulent flesh buthidas.

steps.name: Witte
steps.text: Your Majesty... I completely understand your fury.

steps.name: Witte
steps.text: But you must understand that these old nobles are more willing to stand with you than the industrial nobles, who put clear price tags on their loyalty.

steps.name: Witte
steps.text: You need as many voices on your side as you can at a time like this, when you need to impress the Armies that continue to encroach upon the far shores of Lake Neva.

steps.name: Fyodor
steps.text: And that's their leverage to bargain with me?

steps.name: Fyodor
steps.text: Even my palace can barely afford heating this winter, and they want me to give them Originium to supply that unproductive Katorga Raion?

steps.name: Fyodor
steps.text: Is it those morsels of profit that they're after? No! They simply seek to emphasize their presence to me and make me bow to them. They will not get their wish!

steps.name: Fyodor
steps.text: The Grand Duchess of Far North, the Armies, and these old nobles...

steps.name: Fyodor
steps.text: When did we allow these leeches to our empire? They suck the blood of Ursus, and all it takes is the slightest opportunity for them to proclaim our weakness and claim Grypherburg for themselves!

steps.name: Fyodor
steps.text: Tell me, Witte... tell me that we can still demand their respect, that my assent to their ridiculous demands will not be seen as weakness.

steps.name: Fyodor
steps.text: Tell me you can make those old aristocrats go to war, risk life and limb in battle, and chase the Fourth Army back to where they belong—otherwise, do NOT trouble me with this matter again!

steps.name: Witte
steps.text: Your Imperial Majesty...

steps.name: Fyodor
steps.text: You know, Witte, sometimes, I can't help but think that there is too much rot growing on Ursus, like that Katorga they're so obsessed with protecting, and those people themselves.

steps.name: Witte
steps.text: Your Majesty is certainly correct. The Empire of Ursus is sick. But any doctor can tell you that one must be careful about what medicine to give the very ill.

steps.name: Witte
steps.text: Our Originium reserves are on the brink. You must do everything in your power to stop the forces of sedition from growing within Ursus, until we can come up with a material solution.

steps.name: Witte
steps.text: Otherwise, our internal conflicts will destroy us before any external foe or force of nature.

steps.name: Fyodor
steps.text: Fantastic. Great Ursus is as fragile as a Gaulish omelette, falling apart at the slightest touch.

steps.name: Witte
steps.text: You need not do much.

steps.name: Witte
steps.text: Simply placate them as usual, tell them that Ursus needs their loyalty, and that you intend to protect their interests.

steps.name: Witte
steps.text: I will handle the rest.

steps.name: Fyodor
steps.text: Do whatever you want, Witte.

steps.name: Fyodor
steps.text: I'm used to it. Those bemedaled skeletons and perfumed parasites stand in the way of everything I try to do... they don't care about Ursus, and they certainly don't care about me.

steps.name: Witte
steps.text: You can explain it to them when you attend tonight's ball.

steps.name: Fyodor
steps.text: Can't you and the Vice Chairman go for me? I'm tired.

steps.name: Witte
steps.text: It would be improper, Majesty.

steps.name: Witte
steps.text: You cannot refuse to attend the Winter Ball two years in a row. At a time like this, when people's hearts are unsettled, your subjects look to you to offer some degree of comfort—

steps.name: Fyodor
steps.text: Alright, alright, I'll go, just give me some time, please! That's enough talk. We've had too many vexations this winter already.

steps.name: Fyodor
steps.text: Leave me, Witte... please. And, I'm sorry.

steps.name: Fyodor
steps.text: Blyat! Blyat! Blyat...
Fyodor looks out the window. The streets of Grypherburg are nowhere near as bright as they were years past.

steps.name: Fyodor
steps.text: Such a cold winter... it could really use a fire.

steps.name: Fyodor
steps.text: What's this...? A power outage?

steps.name: Angry Student
steps.text: Death to the mudak tsar! Death to the mudak tsar! Death to the mudak tsar!

steps.name: Angry Student
steps.text: Bring out the bloodsucker Witte! Bring out the imbecile Fyodor!

steps.name: Fyodor
steps.text: You're looking for me? Here I am.

steps.name: Fyodor
steps.text: My, what a commotion.

steps.name: Frightened Student
steps.text: Please! Stop! No more!

steps.name: Tall Policeman
steps.text: Shut up! How dare you insult His Imperial Majesty! Traitor!
He strikes the student's back with such force that his stick flies from his hand, falling by the wayside. Then it is fists and kicks that find their mark...

steps.name: Fyodor
steps.text: Enough, enough! He's not resisting. No need to beat him so hard.

steps.name: Tall Policeman
steps.text: Another traitor to the empire!

steps.name: Fyodor
steps.text: Traitor to the empire? Hah! Whose empire?

steps.name: Tall Policeman
steps.text: Insolent mudak! You need a beating too!

steps.name: Fyodor
steps.text: Such impudence!

steps.name: Tall Policeman
steps.text: How dare you hit me!

steps.name: Fyodor
steps.text: Indeed, I hit you. You may boast to your children that the tsar—
A heavy fist finds Fyodor's face before he can finish.

steps.name: Voice in Earpiece
steps.text: *Bzz*... target... escape... capture, complete! Over!

steps.name: Voice in Earpiece
steps.text: In the name of... *bzz*... His Imperial Majesty! Over!
The concealed communications device that Fyodor carries has fallen on the ground by the time he gets up. With no time to examine it, he quickly grabs it and puts it back in his ear.

steps.name: Fyodor
steps.text: ...Blyat.

steps.name: Voice in Earpiece
steps.text: Mayday! Mayday! Anyone hear me?

steps.name: Voice in Earpiece
steps.text: All Student Assembly members, evacuate immediately! The lead vehicle is driving towards the outskirts!

steps.name: Voice in Earpiece
steps.text: If you can hear me, answer ASAP! Botani out!

steps.name: Fyodor
steps.text: Wait—
Several policemen grab and push him into the crowd that is being packed up into the cramped trucks.
The trucks drive to Katorga Raion, to the sound of frightened crying.

steps.name: Voice in Earpiece
steps.text: And so... we were all captured.

steps.name: Voice in Earpiece
steps.text: No explanations, no promises, no food, no tents.

steps.name: Voice in Earpiece
steps.text: We were tossed into Katorga like garbage.

steps.name: Nervous Student
steps.text: Don't worry! I'll help you!
The diminutive student keeps Fyodor behind him, wildly swinging the tibia of some unidentified beast at the surrounding tuskbeasts.

steps.name: Nervous Student
steps.text: Stay behind me! I've hunted in the Far North with my father! I can handle these beasts! Trust me!

steps.name: Nervous Student
steps.text: Look out!

steps.name: Nervous Student
steps.text: Phew... they're gone. That was close.
He drops to the ground in a pile of snow, panting.

steps.name: Fyodor
steps.text: Your arm. It's hurt.

steps.name: Nervous Student
steps.text: Huh? Argh... you wouldn't happen to have alcohol and bandages on you, would you?

steps.name: Fyodor
steps.text: No. But I'll find you the finest doctors in Grypherburg once we are free of this place.

steps.name: Nervous Student
steps.text: Don't worry about it. It's cold here, maybe it won't get infected.

steps.name: Nervous Student
steps.text: What's your name?

steps.name: Fyodor
steps.text: ...Fyodor.

steps.name: Nervous Student
steps.text: Let me call you Fedya, since I've helped you. You can call me Shorty. That's what my friends call me.

steps.name: Fyodor
steps.text: You don't mind?

steps.name: Shorty
steps.text: Minding doesn't change anything... If you're not hurt, I'll go on ahead.

steps.name: Fyodor
steps.text: Wait, you're going to the wall?

steps.name: Shorty
steps.text: Yes, my friend told me that the one in charge here lets you go if you pay up.

steps.name: Shorty
steps.text: I put together some money. Not sure if it's enough, but I figured I might as well take the chance.

steps.name: Shorty
steps.text: Here, you can have this ration bar. If you need a place to start a fire, the students have a camp down on the south side.

steps.name: Shorty
steps.text: Bye, Fedya—

steps.name: Fyodor
steps.text: ...Wait.

steps.name: Fyodor
steps.text: Take these chervontsy. This should be enough to bribe the guards.
Emotions flash rapidly across Shorty's face. He bows solemnly to Fyodor and walks to the walls.

steps.name: Shorty
steps.text: Please, hear me out—!

steps.name: Voice in Earpiece
steps.text: *Bzz*... this is Botani calling anyone who can hear me. Anyone?

steps.name: Voice in Earpiece
steps.text: Please, do you copy...?

steps.name: Voice in Earpiece
steps.text: The Council of Sixteen thugs are killing students! We need help!

steps.name: Voice in Earpiece
steps.text: Can anyone hear me? Come in, please?

steps.name: Voice in Earpiece
steps.text: Have we been abandoned? Are our cries and screams soundless?

steps.name: Voice in Earpiece
steps.text: It's a wall, not the great tundra! Why...?

steps.name: Voice in Earpiece
steps.text: (Sobs) Why doesn't anyone hear us...?

steps.name: Fyodor
steps.text: What should I...?

steps.name: Voice in Earpiece
steps.text: ...Botani out.

steps.name: Voice in Earpiece
steps.text: (Rasping call) Attempt No. 373. Calling anyone who can hear me...

steps.name: Voice in Earpiece
steps.text: We are trapped in Grypherburg's Katorga Raion, unable to contact anyone on the outside...

steps.name: Voice in Earpiece
steps.text: Yesterday alone, five students died from blunt force trauma and hypothermia... there may have been more. We find ourselves on the brink of death, here in the glorious capital of Ursus.

steps.name: Voice in Earpiece
steps.text: The people who murdered my friends now sit in a room above me...

steps.name: Voice in Earpiece
steps.text: Attempt No. 374. Come in, come in...

steps.name: Voice in Earpiece
steps.text: ...Maybe you'll never be like that voice from the Far North, Botani. You'll never change anything.

steps.name: Voice in Earpiece
steps.text: How could I make people hear my voice, so that all these lives can be saved?

steps.name: Voice in Earpiece
steps.text: (Sound of pained vomiting)

steps.name: Voice in Earpiece
steps.text: (Sobs)

steps.name: Fyodor
steps.text: Three hundred and seventy-four... you have shown more spirit than any bureaucrat in the palaces of Deity Grypherburg.

steps.name: Fyodor
steps.text: Maybe you don't realize it, but you are doing great deeds.

steps.name: Voice in Earpiece
steps.text: ...Huh?

steps.name: Voice in Earpiece
steps.text: Y-You can hear me? Who is this...?

steps.name: Fyodor
steps.text: I... I'm Fedya. I'm from Sonya's camp.

steps.name: Voice in Earpiece
steps.text: Sonya's camp... I know of it, but I couldn't go, no, I didn't dare...

steps.name: Voice in Earpiece
steps.text: I sneaked into the last truck that came here... I wanted to tell the people of Grypherburg the truth of what I saw, the cruelty and brutality that's being inflicted upon the young people here.

steps.name: Voice in Earpiece
steps.text: But nobody answered, nobody heard me... this room I'm hiding in is right in the middle of the thugs' camp...

steps.name: Voice in Earpiece
steps.text: They came in today, and they stabbed the wardrobe that I'm hiding in with a freshly-honed knife... I think I can still hear its blade trembling...

steps.name: Voice in Earpiece
steps.text: I can't come out. They'll get me for sure.

steps.name: Voice in Earpiece
steps.text: (Sobs) I can't do anything—

steps.name: Fyodor
steps.text: In that case...

steps.name: Fyodor
steps.text: Why do you keep talking?

steps.name: Voice in Earpiece
steps.text: ...Why?

steps.name: Fyodor
steps.text: There are thugs all around you. The wise would remain silent and cover their eyes and ears, the wise would ignore everything going on around them...

steps.name: Fyodor
steps.text: What is happening in Katorga had nothing to do with you... you could have remained silent. You live in danger and in pain. No one would blame you.

steps.name: Fyodor
steps.text: Yet you entered the quarantine zone and risked exposure to publicize the tragedies, even though no one is listening. You believe every call you make offers hope to the students.

steps.name: Voice in Earpiece
steps.text: I can... offer hope... the students need...

steps.name: Fyodor
steps.text: Unless you have a better explanation... I've really had quite enough, listening to a brave soul lament her cowardice. I come out here just once and I seem to keep running into this sort of thing.

steps.name: Fyodor
steps.text: How many hostiles on your end?

steps.name: Voice in Earpiece
steps.text: Two.

steps.name: Fyodor
steps.text: Good. Just the two of them won't catch you. Can you hear their movements from your location? Like what they're saying, what shape they're in?

steps.name: Voice in Earpiece
steps.text: ...I can hear, if I listen carefully. They keep complaining about work and yawning. They seem tired.

steps.name: Fyodor
steps.text: Excellent. The tired are less alert. They are people too; they can grow weak or careless. Even you should be able to kill someone who is badly fatigued.

steps.name: Voice in Earpiece
steps.text: That's too—

steps.name: Fyodor
steps.text: Well, it's up to you whether you do it or not. But you can run, can't you?

steps.name: Fyodor
steps.text: Tonight, once they're asleep and you can hear them snoring, run, and don't look back.

steps.name: Fyodor
steps.text: If you don't know the way, I'll guide you. I walked all the way from the wall to the camp. I remember the buildings you'll pass.

steps.name: Fyodor
steps.text: If you try, you'll find that it's not so hard after all.

steps.name: Voice in Earpiece
steps.text: ...Will I continue to hear your voice?

steps.name: Fyodor
steps.text: If it gives you the courage to move...
She recalls the day she decided what she wanted to do with her life.
The smell of dust and dirt, and overheated electronics... she curled up on a chair, searching for news of Bresk—of home, amidst the haphazard and scattered frequencies.
'Next, an excerpt from the opera—'
'Hiss—'
She fiddles with the knob. She needs to hear the sound of hope, a power that brings comfort, to keep the weightless panic in her chess, even for just a moment...

steps.name: Botani
steps.text: —What?
'Bzz, bzzt...'
'Comrades in the mines and cities.'
'We come from the Far North.'

steps.name: Botani
steps.text: ...I'll try.

steps.name: Botani
steps.text: Can I ask who you are? You're not a student, are you?

steps.name: Fyodor
steps.text: ...That is correct, but Sonya permits my presence.

steps.name: Botani
steps.text: I see... I've been providing communications support for the Student Assembly. Any student who hears my voice recognizes me and the code name 'Botani'.

steps.name: Voice From Upstairs
steps.text: Take a break, Pavalo. Even I'm tired after hauling all those crates today, you must be exhausted.

steps.name: Pavalo's Voice
steps.text: It-It's an honor to carry Master Gromov's burdens.

steps.name: Voice From Upstairs
steps.text: Come on, you got a barony from your dad, you could grovel a little bit less.

steps.name: Pavalo's Voice
steps.text: He's long gone, and our family is...

steps.name: Pavalo's Voice
steps.text: Can you tell Gromov, I just want to leave, you guys kidnapped me—

steps.name: Voice From Upstairs
steps.text: Shut it. Yeah, I kidnapped you, big deal. Boss needed someone who was good with numbers. It's not like you've been treated badly.

steps.name: Voice From Upstairs
steps.text: You want to get out, talk less and work harder.

steps.name: Fyodor
steps.text: What is it, Botani?

steps.name: Botani
steps.text: No, it's nothing.

steps.name: Botani
steps.text: It's just that when I get a chance to actually listen to them talk... they don't seem so scary anymore.

steps.name: Fyodor
steps.text: Hmph. I know exactly how many good-for-nothings there are in Ursus.

steps.name: Botani
steps.text: Hehe...

steps.name: Botani
steps.text: Thank you, Fedya.

steps.name: Botani
steps.text: Thank you for hearing my voice.
A cold draft keeps blowing in from the window that will not shut, causing the rickety house to hum quietly in the night.
Sitting in front of a dirty table, Pavalo flips through the ledger to the deafening snores of his colleague in the next room, his brow furrowed.

steps.name: Pavalo
steps.text: How come I haven't seen a shadow of any of the supplies that Gromov requested...?

steps.name: Pavalo
steps.text: No, the purchase price is much higher than the market price, and the Sixteen Warriors' nominal wages are far higher than what they actually are.

steps.name: Pavalo
steps.text: Hmph. A tale as old as Grypherburg itself.
He sneers. At almost the same moment, the roaring snore is interrupted, replaced by a wet, bubbling sound, as though someone is gargling.

steps.name: Pavalo
steps.text: Dreaming about meat again? Mudak sounds like he fell into a soup pot.

spans.text: sounds like he fell into a soup pot.

steps.text: The gurgling ceases, replaced by the sound of liquid dripping on the floor.

steps.name: Pavalo
steps.text: ...A leak?
He rubs his dry eyes and gets up to head over to the next room.
Pavalo opens the door. His pupils contract in shock, and he drops the ledger to the floor. Deep crimson liquid is seeping from his colleague's neck.

steps.name: Pavalo
steps.text: Ahh—

steps.name: Botani
steps.text: Hush... your life is in my hands, Baron.

steps.name: Pavalo
steps.text: Wh-Who are you?

steps.name: Botani
steps.text: Th-That's not important. What's important is that I need your help.

steps.name: Pavalo
steps.text: ...Your voice is trembling, and your hand's trembling even worse. Are you nervous?

steps.name: Pavalo
steps.text: Put down the knife, devushka, and we can talk about this—

steps.name: Botani
steps.text: No...

steps.name: Botani
steps.text: I-If you shout, or try to stall for time, I'll have to kill you.

steps.name: Botani
steps.text: Like you said, my hand's trembling. I can't promise you it won't accidentally slip...

steps.name: Pavalo
steps.text: P-Please, I have a family back home. Spare me, and I'll do anything—

steps.name: Botani
steps.text: ...Put on this headset.

steps.name: Pavalo
steps.text: What...?

steps.name: Botani
steps.text: I won't keep holding you up with a knife, but if you make one wrong move... this headset represents the latest research from the Third Bureau. It can blow your head off your shoulders at any time.

steps.name: Pavalo
steps.text: The Third Bureau?! N-No, how did I get on their bad side—

steps.name: Botani
steps.text: Quiet... someone will tell you where to go through the headset. You will lead me there, avoiding all Sixteen Warriors positions along the way. Do you understand?

steps.name: Pavalo
steps.text: Y-Yes...

steps.name: Voice in Earpiece
steps.text: Tell me where your camp is, I'll head there...

steps.name: Fyodor
steps.text: Ha, haha—

steps.name: Voice in Earpiece
steps.text: ...What's so funny?

steps.name: Fyodor
steps.text: No, it's nothing. First, tell me the buildings you see around your position—
I'm getting my very own 'mission'... this is certainly unexpected, but not entirely unwelcome.
Let me think... how do those Third Bureau freaks talk?
